title: A qargi provider definition or model catalog, schema 2
description: A definition describes ONE runtime on ONE surface (local: a command-line runtime; cloud: a hosted one). A catalog describes the models of a family, shared by every runtime of that family. An extension (a library pack only) adds capabilities and what backs them to ONE runtime on ONE surface: it never overrides anything the runtime or another enabled extension has, and what it provides counts only after `qargi provider check` of the extension (hash-bound to the extension and its runtime). Shipped ones live in lib/providers/NAME.json and lib/providers/catalogs/FAMILY.json; the user's live in the pack library, QARGI_CONF/packs/providers/NAME/definition.json. lib/provider.py validates a document against the node of $defs named by its kind (provider, catalog or extension) with a stdlib subset of JSON Schema (type, enum, const, pattern, required, properties, additionalProperties false, items, minItems, uniqueItems, $ref and the format date) and then checks what a schema cannot say: the name equals the file or directory name, a catalog reference names a catalog, every model matches the pattern, every tier resolves, the paths of the resources stay inside the checkout or the home. Sections whose consumers are built later (renderers, dispatch, barrier) are checked for their discriminator only; their other keys are not yet constrained.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null when not verified

family.description: the family whose catalog this runtime shares and whose name selects it when it is the only runtime of the family on a surface; null for none

capabilities.description: What this runtime can do. A cell is flat (one surface). Omitted means no. yes or partial counts only when verified: shipped, verified_on is set; library, a record bound to the definition's hash in the verification file.

resources.description: Where the runtime keeps what qargi links or reads. A resource that is absent or null is unsupported: the verb that needs it refuses with exit 3.

contract_addenda.description: Text files in the definition's own directory that are added to the member contract of a cloud agent's prompt, in this order (a cloud runtime's rules about its own surface). Each is a relative file name inside the directory, plain text (UTF-8, no control, format, private-use or unassigned characters), at most 16384 bytes; `provider check` fails on one that is missing or is not. Not available to an extension.

agents.description: Agent concepts of the runtime, or null when it has none (members are then composed into the run prompt). qargi's own reserved names (roles, lead, bases) are added by the core.

reserved_names.description: names the runtime's agent concept already uses; a member may not take them

tools.description: neutral tool name to the runtime's name for it

required_tools.description: per member class, the neutral tools that must map

limits.description: length and character limits of names and descriptions

renderers.description: how a neutral definition becomes native files (built later)

home.description: mode command only: a home directory of the member's own, RUN/home/DIR, that qargi local run names in the variable env, with each file `from` (a file under the user's home, ~/PATH) linked into it as `to` for the length of the run. The link is made when the run starts and removed when it ends, its target is never printed and the file is never copied; a source that does not exist is left out with a note. env may not be a variable qargi sets or never hands on (env_pass_problem) nor one of env_pass; dir is a relative path; from may not be qargi's own directory or a credential store of the user's other tools (ssh, gpg, git, forges, clouds, keyrings); to is a plain file name. At most 8 links. Absent or null: the member's home is the run's home and nothing is linked.

run_config.description: mode command only: the MCP file of one member run, rendered by qargi local run when the run starts from resources.mcp (its format, root pointer, entry and tool_lists, which it needs) for the run's role, as the lead's registry of local runs records it, and the run's class: each server lists the tools a member may call (never an always_ask tool, under the read-only class only a declared read). in home: RUN/home/DIR/FILE, the run home of dispatch.home (which it needs), for a runtime that reads its configuration from its home by itself; in run: RUN/config/FILE. {run_config} in argv is the path of the file, and has no value when no tool pack gives the role a tool: nothing is written then, and a file of that name left in the place is removed. --dry-run prints the path and the tool names (RUN_CONFIG=, RUN_CONFIG_TOOLS=), never the file. file is a plain file name and not one of the run home's links. Absent or null: a run gets no MCP file.

output.description: what the command writes on its standard output (OUT/transcript): format text or jsonl (one JSON object per line). usage (jsonl only, with tokens and fields): the lines it picks are the runtime's own report of the tokens a turn used; qargi local run adds up each field over those lines when the run ends, records the sums in RUN/dispatch.json (usage: events, tokens, and model when the rule has it) and prints them as USAGE=; a field no picked line reports is left out of tokens and named in unreported, never recorded as 0. A cost_report claim of a command runtime rests on it.

dispatch.description: how a member is started: in the lead's own session, as a command line, or through the adapter (built later). In the argv of mode command, {final_message} is the file the runtime is told to write the member's last message to: a file of a directory of the run made new for each run (RUN/final.XXXXXXXXXXXX/message.md), never one of OUT. When the process has ended qargi local run takes it only as a regular file with one name, of text, at most 1 MiB (never following a link or waiting on a pipe) and publishes it as OUT/report.md by renaming a new file over that name; the report of an earlier run is set aside as OUT/report.md.previous before the member starts and stays there when the run publishes none.

barrier.description: how a read-only member is held (built later); absent or kind none: nothing holds it

launch.description: the command that starts an interactive session on a render; {render} is the render directory. A group in [...] is kept only when the file named by its last word exists

render_target.description: the --target name the packs renderer answers to; absent or null: the runtime has no packs renderer of its own, and the verb that needs one is refused with exit 3

notes.description: How this runtime does what a skill asks of it, as short topics (a topic name to its text), read with the notes verb of provider so the skills stay free of any runtime's words. At most 16 topics; a topic is a lower case name (letters, digits and -, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters); a text is one line of plain text (no control, format, private-use or unassigned character), not empty, at most 2000 characters. Not available to an extension. A library pack's notes are part of the definition, so the seal hash covers them.

adapter.description: an executable relative to the definition's directory (no .. and no absolute path); called as adapter VERB with a JSON request on stdin

adapter_verbs.description: the verbs the adapter serves; absent means every verb of the adapter contract

extension.description: What a project adds to a runtime, enabled per project (models.extensions of its answers). extends is a runtime name or a family name; the extension applies on ONE surface: surface, or the only surface of the runtime it names (an extension that names a family says its surface). Enabled extensions are merged onto the runtime in name order; a key that the runtime or another enabled extension already has is a conflict and the composition is refused, nothing is ever overridden. provides must equal the capability names of adds.capabilities. requires must hold on the runtime alone, or the extension is ignored with its reason shown.

capabilities.description: capabilities the runtime must have verified (yes or partial) without this extension

renderers.description: renderer name to renderer; a name the runtime already has is a conflict

variants.description: variant name to a dispatch variant; the runtime must have a dispatch

barrier.description: only for a runtime whose barrier is absent or none

adapter_verbs.description: adapter verb to an executable inside the pack; a verb the runtime's adapter serves, or another extension adds, is a conflict

version.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the last change; a change makes every render that includes the catalog stale

pattern.description: a regular expression every model id must match

models.description: Either {catalog, use} (the models of a family's catalog) or the inline form {pattern, tiers, effort}; not both.

use.description: alias: the tier's alias when it has one, else its id; id: always the id

tiers.description: tier to model. * fills every tier not given, so a single-model runtime writes only *. Every tier must resolve.

effort.description: qargi's effort level to the runtime's own value; null (or a level that is null or absent) means no such control

exclusion.description: how the runtime's own configuration switches an item off (qargi only reads it). form selects which of the other keys apply; null: none

off.description: the value that means off: a string for settings-key, an object for config-list

project_file.description: file names in order of preference

res_mcp.description: the file the runtime reads its MCP servers from and what it calls a tool of one. permission_rule is the form of a tool's name, with {server} for the name of the tool pack and {tool} for the tool: the render writes its permission rules in it, a member's tool list holds its tools under it, and the guard takes a call of a tool whose name has this form for an MCP call. name_key says how the runtime writes a server or a tool name inside it: nonword-underscore replaces every character that is not an ASCII letter, a digit, _ or - by _; null or absent leaves a name as written. format is how the file is written: json, or toml (tables, texts, whole numbers, booleans and lists of texts; the entry template may hold nothing else). tool_lists is for a runtime that takes the tools of a server in the server's entry: allow and deny are JSON pointers into the entry; allow gets the tools a member may call for the roles the pack reaches (never an always_ask tool, under the read-only class only a declared read), deny the pack's other tools, and a server with an allow list and no tool on it is left out. It needs a permission_rule with {server} and {tool}, since the member policy judges a tool by that name

files.description: the settings files a session reads, lowest scope first; user paths start with ~/, the others are relative to the checkout

res_transcripts.description: where the runtime keeps the transcripts of its sessions (a file of JSON lines per session, named for the session id, in user_dir; {checkout_key} as for memory) and how to read the context in use from one. usage names JSON pointers into one line: select and skip are maps from a pointer to the value that picks a line (select) or drops it (skip); tokens points at the object holding the counts, fields lists the counts that add up to the context in use, model points at the model id. window is the context window in tokens that is assumed when the answer lead.context_window is not set and no entry of windows matches the model id; windows is a list, first match wins, of {model, tokens}: model is a pattern for the whole model id in which * stands for any run of characters and every other character is itself (case does not matter), tokens the window of a model that matches.

usage.description: how to read token counts from a file of JSON lines: select and skip are maps from a JSON pointer to the value that picks a line (select, every one must match) or drops it (skip); tokens points at the object holding the counts, fields lists the counts read from it, model points at the model id

res_memory.description: the runtime's own memory directory for a checkout. {checkout_key} in user_dir is replaced by the key the rule makes of the checkout's absolute path: nonalnum-dash replaces every character that is not a letter or digit by -; sha256-16 is the first 16 hex digits of the sha256 of the path; none is the empty string
